Enable experimental DNS filtering?

Hisn checks supported IPv4 UDP and TCP DNS requests to its virtual DNS server against the bundled list and your saved rules. Allowed requests go to Cloudflare Families (1.1.1.3) over authenticated, encrypted DNS-over-TLS. Cloudflare can see these requests. Hisn does not save a browsing log or fall back to plaintext DNS.

Android allows one VPN per profile. Starting Hisn can disconnect your existing VPN.

Hisn answers well-known encrypted-DNS provider names and Firefox’s DNS-over-HTTPS canary domain with “not found”. This reduces, but does not stop, apps using their own encrypted DNS: some reach providers at built-in IP addresses. This DNS layer also does not cover direct IP access, cached answers, images or videos. Optional visual checks are a separate layer. TCP is bounded to DNS port 53 and messages up to 4096 bytes; unsupported requests or resolver failures can interrupt loading. Client TLS on port 853 is refused so Android uses port 53 instead. If Android Private DNS is set to a provider hostname, system DNS can bypass Hisn; Hisn warns but does not change that setting. Always-on and lockdown are unsupported. If you leave DNS filtering on, Hisn starts it again after a restart while Android still holds this VPN approval. You can disconnect through Android VPN settings.

Hisn will use Android accessibility screenshots to inspect the active window of apps you explicitly select for inspection. A bundled adult-image model processes downscaled samples on this device. Samples are not saved or uploaded. No camera or microphone is used.

Screenshots can contain private images and messages. Hisn pauses when an identified editable or password field is focused, but sensitive content may still appear elsewhere. Select only apps you want captured.

A sample is requested about every two seconds while a selected app is active, with one request at a time. Flagged samples return you to Home with a restriction notice. This restricts the whole app screen; it does not blur individual images or pause individual videos. Content can appear before intervention. Small images, short video frames, secure windows and classification mistakes leave gaps. Unknown samples are not marked clean. Android 14+ is required.

Allow protection in selected apps?

Hisn uses Android accessibility to identify selected apps and inspect their visible text. If you separately enable image/video checks, Hisn also takes transient screenshots of selected app windows; review that option’s separate disclosure in Rules. Your app restrictions, daily schedule or matching words can return you to the home screen and show a restriction notice.

Text is processed on this device and is not saved or sent to a server. Input fields, password fields and their child elements are skipped where Android identifies them. Some sensitive text may still appear in ordinary labels or messages. Select only apps you want inspected.

This cannot read every app or guarantee a block before content appears. Hisn does not use accessibility to prevent uninstalling or disabling services. Enable Hisn manually in the next settings screen if you agree.

Applies your chosen permanent or scheduled app restrictions and checks visible text in selected apps. It skips identified text input and password fields. Separately enabled visual checks sample selected windows and pause while an identified input is focused. Text and pixels stay on your device and are not saved. Enable only after reviewing the disclosure in Hisn.

Commitment time counts while the device is running, including after a restart. Time while the device is switched off is not counted, so powering off extends the period; Hisn does not trust a changed date. Daily schedules instead follow the device clock and time zone, which can still be changed outside Hisn.

Check the DNS route
Run these checks

Hisn sends a synthetic blocked .invalid query, then example.com if the block passes, first over UDP and then over one reused TCP connection through the virtual DNS route. That is four fixed queries when all checks pass. Allowed queries reach Cloudflare Families over the authenticated TLS resolver connection. No adult site is requested.\n\nThis tests the local UDP/TCP DNS route, not every app, encrypted content or all traffic. Queries are not sent automatically after network changes. DNS setup and Android VPN consent are separate steps.

Protection
Rules
Guide
Reduce exposure to adult content and support the boundaries you choose.
The goal of Hisn

Help you avoid adult websites, explicit text and flagged images or sampled video frames, restrict distracting apps, and keep your chosen boundaries during a commitment. You choose the layers and apps. Hisn reports what is running and what needs attention.
Set up your protection

1. In Rules, choose blocked apps, a daily schedule, or apps to inspect. Built-in adult-text and image/video checks are separate optional layers.

2. Review the accessibility disclosure and enable Hisn in Android settings for app restrictions or inspections. Image/video checks need Android 14+.

3. In Protection, review DNS filtering and approve the Android VPN request for domain blocking. Another VPN may disconnect.

4. Run the DNS route check and review each layer’s status. A passed check verifies only that DNS path.

5. Once your rules are ready, optionally choose a commitment in Rules. Hisn rejects weaker saved restrictions during that period.
Understand the coverage

DNS blocks matching domains on the supported route. Independent encrypted DNS, cached answers and direct IP connections can bypass it. Text and visual checks inspect only selected apps and may act after content appears. Visual checks classify downscaled window samples, not every image or video frame. Secure windows cannot be inspected.\n\nAndroid can stop services or revoke permissions. Reopen Protection after a restart or permission change. Commitments guard changes inside Hisn; Android settings, data clearing and uninstall remain available. This build does not provide always-on or lockdown VPN protection.
